title: Internal import alias requirement conflicts with isolated source-copy resolution
symptom: The user expected internal imports to share a project alias. Tests and development tools use @/, while product engine imports remain relative and import alignment does not rewrite module specifiers.

rootCause.summary: The former repository contract forbade @/ in product sources because only the root tsconfig defined it and isolated development copies lacked equivalent resolution. The migration added the copied-skill mapping, dependency isolation, alias-aware layout enforcement and bundled resolution before changing engine imports.

requestedOutcome: Use configured aliases consistently for internal source imports with equivalent module resolution in development copy and release bundles, preserving package boundaries and execution order.
decisions: The 2026-10-21 user request adds alias consistency to AUTHOR1 and the Write/Refactor skill.
An alias is not an OS absolute path. Keep the existing @/* engine-root meaning during investigation.
Migrate the resolver, checker and installation contracts together before changing product imports; horizontal Align never rewrites module specifiers.
Keep the engine-external rules JSON import and the three import.meta.url runtime paths relative because they are outside the engine module alias contract.

actions.description: Record alias-aware authoring guidance and explicit migration acceptance work.
Inventory imports and make isolated copy plus bundle resolution support internal source aliases.
Migrate imports and associated repository/checker contracts, then verify equivalent source-copy and bundle resolution.
Complete the final independent READINESS1 audit that includes the migrated source state.

verification.name: Portable alias migration
verification.scope: Repository-wide source migration, isolated copy execution and installed release bundles after migration.
verification.result: All 169 engine-internal module specifiers use @/; the AST inventory retains only the engine-external rules JSON import and three runtime URL paths. Isolated copied-skill TypeScript/JSON/YAML execution, Node bundle smoke, public and installer artifacts, and the final check (629 pass, 5 pre-existing parser-toolchain skips, 0 fail) succeeded. Three pre-existing non-whitespace layout refusals in Kotlin, Rust and Swift profiles remain recorded and unchanged.

verification.name: Requirement and skill consistency
verification.scope: Alias guidance and pending migration acceptance only; no implemented source migration or release verdict.
verification.result: Scoped Sonnet and GLM reviews passed after precedence clarification. Plugin contract tests and plugin guard passed within the recorded scope.

related.note: Allows existing engine-root aliases, rejects invalid targets and prevents new unintended relative engine module imports.
Copies the skill-local alias config and pinned runtime dependencies with ownership-safe lifecycle handling.
Normalized imports after the bounded AST module-specifier migration; Align itself remains whitespace-only.
Pins alias targets, the explicit rules-data exception and Windows-safe containment.

history.summary: User reported missing @ alias consistency and requested a remaining-work summary.
Inspection established the existing alias prohibition, engine-root mapping and copy-install boundary; this is not evidence of a completed migration.
Add the requirement to authoring guidance and AUTHOR1; implement resolver and import changes together in subsequent work.
Sonnet identified ambiguity between alias guidance and the retained product-source prohibition. The subsequent pass required explicit project-contract precedence and plan wording.
Clarified guidance and pending acceptance work passed scoped Sonnet/GLM review. Migration remains open and unimplemented.

Added copied-skill alias and dependency isolation, migrated 169 engine-internal module specifiers to the engine-root alias, and enforced the remaining relative-import boundary with one rules-data exception.

Copied-source execution, bundle and artifact isolation, Windows-safe containment and the final repository check (629 pass, 5 pre-existing parser-toolchain skips, 0 fail) verified the migration. The issue remains verifying until the final READINESS1 independent audit covers this source state.

Closed the bounded implementation with the post-native-fix 632-pass repository check, scoped GLM final audit and supplementary hash/test review. Prior failures and pre-closure verification lists are retained; native host acceptance, rule approvals and publication are separate.
